habitat: Single birds or loose groups on inland waters, seldom large rivers. They dive often and skitter across the water when chasing rivals. The family notes say they are seldom seen on land and fly long distances at night to new waters.
summary: A common resident, smaller than any duck. Dark brown above. In breeding plumage the face and neck are chestnut, with a creamy spot at the base of the bill. At other times the underparts are dull, not white, and the eyes are dark. The identification line also says pale below. The call is a descending, laughing trill. Chicks are striped on the upperparts and ride on the parents’ backs. The Kemp paper name Dabchick and the code VB were left unchanged.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark the Kruger occurrence rare or accidental, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The Kemp code VB and the paper name Dabchick were left unchanged. The identification line says pale below, and the description says the underparts are dull, not white, at other times. The dark eye colour is not named. Sexes were not separated. No non-breeding photograph and no flight photograph were found. The grade A call is from the Eastern Cape. Black-necked Grebe is the comparison Newman gives, and it is not in this list. Great Crested Grebe and Eared Grebe are on the Avibase Kruger list and were not added.
